jj.badge.divergentTip: This change id names more than one commit: refer to this one by its commit id. Combwork never picks one.
jj.bookmarks.name: Bookmark
jj.bookmarks.note: Bookmarks are created, moved and pushed with jj itself: Combwork only shows them.
jj.compare.ambiguous: {rev} names {n, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}}: pick one by its commit id.
jj.compare.bad: Type a bookmark, a change id or a commit id.
jj.compare.capped: The diff is long: only its start is shown.
jj.compare.files: {n, plural, =0 {No files changed} one {# file changed} other {# files changed}}
jj.conflicts.files: {n, plural, one {# conflicted file} other {# conflicted files}}
jj.conflicts.intro: jj can keep a conflict in a commit and carry on. These commits store conflicts; resolve them with jj in a terminal (jj resolve).
jj.history.capped: Only the latest {n, number} are shown.
jj.integrate.head: Waiting for you to integrate
jj.integrate.how: For example, then move {target} to the rebased commit with jj bookmark set:
jj.integrate.noMerge: Combwork doesn’t merge under jj: integrate the reviewed work with jj yourself.
jj.ops.added: {n, plural, one {# commit made} other {# commits made}}: {ids}
jj.ops.command: Undoing it changes only what it changed. To undo it, run this in the project folder:
jj.ops.did: What it changed (undoing it puts these back)
jj.ops.didNothing: Nothing that undoing it would change.
jj.ops.hidden: {n, plural, one {# commit hidden} other {# commits hidden}}: {ids}
jj.ops.intro: jj records every command as an operation. Preview one to see what undoing it would change. Combwork changes nothing here: when undoing it would touch nothing else, it gives you the command to run yourself.
jj.ops.kind.head: Head commit {name}
jj.ops.later: Later work undoing it would also change
jj.ops.movedAtCopy: The repository changed since this preview, so nothing was copied. Here it is again: look at it before copying.
jj.ops.previewAt: A preview at operation {at}. If anything else changes before you run it, preview again: this isn’t a guarantee about a later command.
jj.ops.previewSnapshot: Run in the project folder, jj first records any edits you haven’t recorded yet, as its own operation, then undoes this one.
jj.ops.refused.bounds: it changed more than a preview shows.
jj.ops.refused.gitOwn: it recorded a change made in Git: undoing it changes nothing in Git, and jj would import it again.
jj.ops.refused.heads: jj’s operation log has more than one head.
jj.ops.refused.moved: the repository changed since the preview.
jj.ops.refused.overlap: undoing it would also change later work, listed above.
jj.ops.refused.parents: it joins operations that ran at the same time (or is the first one), so undoing it can’t be previewed.
jj.ops.refused.shape: jj recorded it in a form Combwork can’t read whole.
jj.ops.refused.stale: the project folder’s workspace is stale. jj workspace update-stale updates it, but edits jj hasn’t recorded can end up in a separate commit.
jj.ops.refused.tool: jj isn’t the version Combwork is tested with.
jj.ops.refused.unimported: Git has changes jj hasn’t recorded yet (a branch, a tag or HEAD moved with git): your jj command would take them in first. Run any jj command, then preview again.
jj.ops.refused.workingCopy: it changed a workspace’s working copy: undoing it would update files there, which a preview can’t check.
jj.ops.why.descendant: Commit {commit} was made on top of what it made: undoing it would rebase that commit
jj.ops.why.restored: Commit {commit} it hid is back since
jj.ops.why.rewritten: Commit {commit} it made was rewritten or abandoned since
jj.repo.colocated: {colocated, select, yes {Colocated with Git: Git sees the same history.} other {Not colocated with Git.}}
jj.repo.edits: jj has no uncommitted changes: edits are recorded in the working-copy commit when jj snapshots them.
jj.repo.staleTip: Its files are behind its working-copy commit: another workspace rewrote it. jj workspace update-stale updates them, but edits jj hasn’t recorded can end up in a separate commit: look before you run it. Combwork doesn’t run it.
jj.repo.unsupported: Not supported with jj in Combwork
jj.unknown.heads: jj’s operation log has {detail} heads: Combwork reads nothing until jj reconciles them (any jj command in a terminal does).
jj.unknown.moved: The repository changed while it was read: refresh to read it again.
jj.unknown.noRepo: No jj repository was found here.
jj.unknown.tool: jj isn’t installed, or isn’t the version Combwork is tested with, so nothing is read through it.
